sentences.text: Researchers conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 533 amyloid-positive individuals, 148 of whom met the Boston criteria for probable cerebral amyloid angiopathy, to compare groups based on these specific diagnostic standards.

Analysis revealed that the probable CAA group exhibited higher cortical amyloid accumulation on brain imaging and a stronger association between lower cerebrospinal fluid amyloid-beta levels and a greater burden of lobar microbleeds.

The authors conclude that probable CAA reflects a heavier amyloid load rather than a distinct clinical category with unique symptoms, suggesting that specific imaging markers like superficial siderosis may offer more utility than current classification systems.
